name: A team needs depth on hidden stakeholder needs, agreement between stakeholders, and evidence of actual working habits. Which elicitation choices fit these needs?

answers.body: Use interviews to explore needs in depth.

answers.body: Use facilitated workshops to help stakeholders agree on requirements.

answers.body: Prefer questionnaires over interviews whenever deep answers are required.

answers.body: Observe users at work to discover differences between reported and actual practice.

answers.body: Document analysis examines existing manuals, regulations, forms, and specifications.

answers.body: Reverse engineering and interface analysis examine existing systems and required connections.

answers.body: Prototypes let users react to concrete mockups or working examples.

answers.body: Focus groups collect feedback from a representative group of users.

name: Sketch a conceptual UML fragment for the public transport company. A dispatcher creates daily work schedules connected to lines and their line schedules. Drivers can be licensed for vehicles independently of current driving assignments; vehicles include buses, trams, and trolleybuses. Show the separate concepts and relationships, then identify requirements questions needed before fixing driving-assignment multiplicities and history.
answer: Use conceptual entities Dispatcher, DailyWorkSchedule, Line, LineSchedule, Driver, and Vehicle. Associate DailyWorkSchedule with Line, and Line with LineSchedule; keep the two schedule concepts distinct. Bus, Tram, and TrolleyBus specialize Vehicle. Label the dispatcher-schedule relation creates and keep has license separate from drives between Driver and Vehicle. The supplied example shows a many-to-many license relation. Clarify when a driving assignment is made, whether drivers select a free vehicle or have a regular vehicle, how many drivers and vehicles participate, how permanent assignments are, and which history must be retained. Ask who manages vehicle records and whether removal from service and its history belong inside the system boundary. Draw conceptual information rather than implementation methods or database keys.
keyPoints: Includes the stated schedule, line, driver, dispatcher, and vehicle concepts, with Vehicle specializations.
Includes DailyWorkSchedule-Line and Line-LineSchedule associations while keeping the schedule concepts distinct.
Distinguishes qualification has license from actual driving assignments rather than merging the two.
Uses association names, endpoint roles, and justified or explicitly provisional multiplicities.
Raises timing, permanence, history, and ownership questions for assignments.
Raises record management and vehicle-removal system-boundary questions; avoids methods and implementation attributes.
source: 02-03-Analysis-patterns.pdf, slides 7-10; public-transport.pdf, pages 2-3 (Use Case Model and Problem Domain Model). Practical synthesis from these diagrams; unresolved driving policy remains an elicitation question.

name: Draw a UML class fragment and object example for two simultaneous structures. In Sale, the Brno sales office reports to Moravia and the Prague sales office to Bohemia. In PublicRelations, both offices report to Central. Use Organization Structure so the offices are shared between the two structures.
answer: Model OrganizationStructureType and OrganizationStructure. Each structure-link object has one type and two Organization endpoints named parent and subsidiary. Use Organization subtypes SalesOffice, Division, and OperatingUnit as needed. Create shared Organization objects Brno and Prague, Division objects Moravia and Bohemia, and OperatingUnit object Central. Create Sale and PublicRelations type objects. The four link objects are Sale(parent=Moravia, subsidiary=Brno), Sale(parent=Bohemia, subsidiary=Prague), PublicRelations(parent=Central, subsidiary=Brno), and PublicRelations(parent=Central, subsidiary=Prague). Add applicable type-specific rules separately rather than requiring a single parent across both structures. The pattern also provides a place for link context such as a TimePeriod when needed.
keyPoints: Reifies each typed parent-subsidiary relationship as OrganizationStructure.
Creates Sale and PublicRelations type instances, not separate classes or fixed associations for each concrete hierarchy.
Reuses the same Brno and Prague Organization objects in both structures.
Shows all four links with the required parents and types.
Keeps applicable constraints and additional relationship context explicit.
source: 02-03-Analysis-patterns.pdf, slides 35-38 (Multiple Organization Hierarchies and Organization Structure exercise); public-transport.pdf, page 5 (motivation to switch when multiple hierarchies or temporal changes appear).

name: Extend a public transport responsibility model for workplace assignment and work distribution. A driver may have a temporary second-depot assignment, and an accident investigation needs to reconstruct the assignments valid at the accident time. Sketch Party and Accountability with a knowledge level. Use the lecture's orientation in which workplace-assignment rules pair an employee parent with a depot child. Show example rules for Driver-Depot and Technician-Depot assignments, Dispatcher-Driver and DepotManager-Technician work distribution. Explain how the model changes if a responsibility belongs to a post whose holder may change.
answer: Keep Party and Accountability on the operational level. Every Accountability has two Party endpoints, an AccountabilityType, and a TimePeriod to preserve its validity interval. Store the temporary second-depot assignment as another dated Accountability rather than overwriting the first depot reference; inspect the intervals at the accident time. At the knowledge level, create PartyTypes Driver, Technician, Dispatcher, DepotManager, and Depot, plus AccountabilityTypes WorkplaceAssignment and WorkDistribution. Give WorkplaceAssignment connection rules for (Driver, Depot) and (Technician, Depot), and WorkDistribution rules for (Dispatcher, Driver) and (DepotManager, Technician), using the stated parent-child orientation consistently. Concrete parties and dated links instantiate these rules. Discuss authorization explicitly and decide whether developers maintain the knowledge-level rules or users must configure them through the UI. If accountability and scope should survive a change of holder, represent Post as another Party type and attach the stable responsibility to it, distinguishing the current holder from the post.
keyPoints: Separates knowledge-level types and connection rules from concrete operational Party and Accountability instances.
Models both Party endpoints, link type, and dated validity for each Accountability.
Preserves concurrent temporary assignments and can examine their validity at the incident time.
Shows all four requested permitted type pairings with a consistent parent-child orientation.
Distinguishes a post and its stable responsibilities from the person currently holding it.
Recognizes authorization and runtime-configuration decisions as questions that affect the system boundary.
source: 02-03-Analysis-patterns.pdf, slides 16, 39-48; public-transport.pdf, pages 6-8 (Accountability motivation, pattern, and knowledge-level diagram). Practical extension includes the temporary-assignment requirement from slide 16.
